## What We'll Build Today {.smaller}

[Outline · Day 02]{.eyebrow}

### From single genes to whole genomes

Yesterday we plotted single experiments and single contrasts. Today we *zoom out*: the unit of analysis is no longer one gene or one sample, it is **the genome itself**. Each chart in this deck answers a question that only makes sense at that scale.

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
- **Stacked bars** — composition of mixtures (admixture, microbiome)
- **Time series** — trajectories with uncertainty
- **MSA** — letters that line up across sequences
- **Manhattan** — significance across the whole genome
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
- **Genome stats** — coverage, peaks, gene models
- **pyCirclize** — circular genome plots
- **Synteny** — comparing genomes side-by-side

::: {.takeaway}
[Today's promise]{.tl}
Every chart starts from a tidy `pandas` DataFrame and grows **one annotated line at a time**. Read the comments — they're the lesson.
:::
:::
::::

## The Setup Cell {.smaller}

[Logistics · Day 02]{.eyebrow}

### One install, then everything works

`genomics_course` ships every loader, the Economist theme, and the matplotlib `rcParams`. Run this once per Colab/Jupyter session, then every later cell just imports.

```bash
pip install -q "git+https://github.com/loukesio/dataviz-genomicsdata.git@Python_2026"
```

```{.python code-line-numbers="1-3|5-9|11-13"}
# the theme registers IBM Plex Mono, defines the Economist palette
# (GREEN, BLUE, AMBER, RED, PURPLE + neutrals), and applies the
# cream-canvas matplotlib rcParams. One import, deck-wide consistency.
from genomics_course.theme import *

from genomics_course.data import (
    load_gwas, load_admixture, load_qc,
    load_peaks, load_peak_genes, load_timecourse,
)                                                # the loaders we'll use today

import numpy as np, pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt, seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.patches as mpatches            # for synteny ribbons later
```
